solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Jazzer rap, strong, was confused? Make do with inferior stuff (13, three words)

indicators.note: something confused is muddled, so the letters of the last word lose their order

blocks.note: a cat is old slang for a jazz musician or fan
a rap is a talk or chat
STR is the standard abbreviation for strong
the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A jazz rapper with a strong voice was baffled by the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs the first four words together as one muddled performer; each is its own piece, and only the last is jumbled. The answer is a variant of clutch at straws.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch at straws is to grasp at any poor expedient going, settling for whatever scrap of help is available.

clue.text: Number entering crypt go dancing – that's plenty (11, three words)

indicators.note: something entering goes into the middle of what follows
dancing letters jump about and land in a new order

blocks.note: the two words rearranged
nine is a number

explanation.surface: A dance number performed inside a church crypt, which someone thinks is quite enough.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from the Bible story of Joseph, where Egypt alone had grain stored for the famine.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn in Egypt is a proverbial phrase for an abundant supply, from Joseph's stored harvests in Genesis.

clue.text: Command after advance poet's tolerated

indicators.note: after says the order comes second, behind the shortened word for moving forward

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for advance
to bid is to command

explanation.surface: An order given after the troops advance has been put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the command comes second. ABID is an old poetic past tense of abide, as Spenser used it.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to put up with, and ABID is the archaic past form found in verse, hence the poet's.

clue.text: Cheap nip drunk within another such

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger and fall into a different order
within says the jumbled word sits inside the next one

blocks.note: the word rearranged
a tot is another small measure of spirits, like a nip

explanation.surface: A cheap drink knocked back on top of another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such' points back to nip: the container is another small drink of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot describes something shoddy and worthless, as cheap as a tin pot.

clue.text: Former monarch after foreign festival growing in sanctimony

indicators.note: after says the old ruler is placed second, behind the celebration abroad

blocks.note: Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late queen

explanation.surface: An old king grows more pious after attending a festival abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the monarch second.
explanation.definitionFit: Holier-than-thou people are sanctimonious, so the comparative describes someone becoming more self-righteous.

clue.text: Old pub sign cut up and put in a shelter

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top
put in tells you the turned word goes inside the shelter

blocks.note: taken as written
a lee is shelter from the wind
to lop is to cut

explanation.surface: An old inn sign was chopped up and stored away in a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: An ale-pole was a pole set up outside an alehouse as its sign, an archaic term.

clue.text: In this is matching kitchen feature by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says we go by how the words are spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: a sink is fitted in every kitchen

explanation.surface: A matching kitchen fitting is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a phrase: things that are 'in sync' match each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in sync means being in step, so the word fills the gap in that idiom for matching.

clue.text: Lecherous old expression he left out of the cable, …

indicators.note: left out of says two letters are dropped from the word that follows

blocks.note: the word with its last two letters gone, as in the dialect contraction t'
a wire is a cable

explanation.surface: An old leer of a man is pulled out of the wiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is not a person but the letters dropped from the following word. TWIRE is an archaic word for a leer or sly glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A twire is an old word for a peep or leer, the expression on a lecherous face.

clue.text: … Typical of this, right – right in a tone of voice?

indicators.note: in places the second letter inside the tone of voice

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
a key is a tone or pitch of voice
R again, for the second right

explanation.surface: Continuing 7: lechery is spoken of in a knowing tone.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 7, so 'this' is the lecherous behaviour there. Rakery is the conduct of a rake, a dissolute man.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a debauchee, and rakery is his dissolute behaviour, so it is typical of lechery.

clue.text: Trick I cast for a fish, not requiring a swim

indicators.note: cast for means thrown out in exchange for something else

blocks.note: a wile is a trick
taken as written: the letter to be swapped out
taken as written
a dab is a small flatfish

explanation.surface: An angler casts for a fish in water shallow enough to stand in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like fishing, but it is the letter I being thrown out of the trick and replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Wadable water is shallow enough to walk through, so you can cross it without swimming.

clue.text: What's Scots rock containing within there? Sparkle

indicators.note: containing means the first word holds the second inside it

blocks.note: sclate is the Scots form of slate, a rock
intil is Scots for in or within

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a Scottish stone with something embedded in it, then a flash of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's Scots' applies to both pieces: each is a Scots word, and 'there' refers to Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To scintillate is to give off sparks or flashes, so it means to sparkle.

clue.text: Funeral ceremonies over, had a snack afterwards

blocks.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
bit is the past tense of bite, to take a mouthful

explanation.surface: Once the funeral was over, the mourners had a bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Obit usually means a death notice, but it also has the old sense of the funeral rites themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An obit is an archaic word for the rites performed at a burial or a memorial service.

clue.text: Figurine from Egypt protected by law

indicators.note: something protected by another is surrounded and enclosed by it

blocks.note: a statute is a law
ET is the international vehicle registration code for Egypt

explanation.surface: An ancient Egyptian figurine is shielded by heritage law.
explanation.definitionFit: A statuette is a small statue, which is what a figurine is.

clue.text: Mathematical calculator one required to divide basic rudiments

indicators.note: to divide something is to split it by going into its middle

blocks.note: the ABC of a subject is its basics
A means one, as the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A calculating device is needed to split the elementary numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: ABAC is the old term for a nomogram, a chart for doing calculations.
explanation.definitionFit: An abac is a nomogram, a graphic device for working out mathematical calculations without arithmetic.

clue.text: Fairy dance, right round fireplace

indicators.note: round says the first piece goes around the second

blocks.note: RT is a standard abbreviation for right
an ingle is a fireplace or hearth

explanation.surface: Fairies dance in a circle around the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: Ringlet more often means a curl of hair; here it is the old word for a fairy ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is an archaic word for a fairy ring, the circle that fairies were said to dance in.

clue.text: Group from the kindergarten going round famous Louvre exhibit?

indicators.note: a group from the phrase is a run of letters taken out of it
going round means turning back, so the run reads backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A school party of small children walks round a famous Louvre exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: the Winged Victory of Samothrace in the Louvre is a statue of the goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winged Victory statue in the Louvre represents Nike, Greek goddess of victory, so it is a fair example.

clue.text: Oriental lute: father accompanies one on piano

blocks.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
I is the Roman numeral one
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad accompanies someone on the piano with a Chinese lute.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'one on piano' puts the I after the P; father joins at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipa is a four-stringed Chinese lute played upright, an oriental instrument of that family.

clue.text: Islander finding odd bits to eat in freshly landed herring

indicators.note: odd bits are the first, third and later odd-numbered characters
in places the chosen letters inside the herring measure

blocks.note: a cran is a measure of fresh herrings landed in port, about 750 fish
the first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: An islander tucks into odd morsels of freshly landed herring.
explanation.walkthrough: The measure is the cran, a fishing-port unit for herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cretan is a native of Crete, an island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Underground feature like others, so mixed up with eight more

indicators.note: mixed up letters are scrambled into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An underground feature resembles others, and so is confused with eight more of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like others' belongs to the definition: an isogeotherm joins points of the same temperature as its neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: An isogeotherm is an imaginary line below the earth's surface linking points of equal temperature.

clue.text: Mogul governor, one clothed in absurd frippery

indicators.note: something clothed in another is wrapped inside it
frippery is frivolous show, so the word is treated lightly and rearranged

blocks.note: the word rearranged
A means one

explanation.surface: A Mughal governor arrives dressed in ridiculous finery.
explanation.definitionFit: A subadar was a provincial governor under the Mughal empire in India, later an Indian army officer rank.

clue.text: Start, often illegally, house with 7

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
the answer to 7 down

explanation.surface: Breaking into a house and starting something you shouldn't.
explanation.definitionFit: To hot-wire a car is to start the engine by bypassing the ignition, usually when stealing it.

clue.text: Barrel rolling weirdo

indicators.note: something rolling turns over, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a tun is a large barrel

explanation.surface: An oddball is rolling a barrel along.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is slang for a crazy or eccentric person, the same as a weirdo.

clue.text: One pursuing topsy-turvy life – tranquillizer required

indicators.note: topsy-turvy means upside down, so in a down clue the word reads from the bottom
pursuing means chasing behind, so the single item comes after the other piece

blocks.note: vita is Latin for life
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Someone whose life is in chaos needs a sedative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pursuing' puts the one after the life piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ativan is a trade name for lorazepam, a benzodiazepine prescribed as a sedative.

clue.text: Members of the goosefoot family – wild astilbe's not one

indicators.note: not one means a single letter standing for one is removed
wild letters run free and settle in a new order

blocks.note: the plant name with its A, meaning one, removed

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that a wild astilbe is not related to the goosefoots.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits one plant against another, but the astilbe supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blite is a name for several plants of the goosefoot family, such as strawberry blite.

clue.text: Clay became this – a red blob fashioned with it is Della-Robbia

indicators.note: something fashioned is shaped anew, so the letters are remade into another form
saying the blob together with the answer makes the name means the name minus the blob leaves the answer

blocks.note: the Florentine family of terracotta sculptors, the full set of letters
taken as written: the letters accounted for, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: Clay became a sculpture: a red blob shaped into a Della Robbia terracotta.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus the letters of a red blob rearrange to Della-Robbia, the Florentine family famed for glazed terracotta, so clay works both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxer Cassius Clay changed his name to Muhammad Ali in 1964.

clue.text: Call for progress demanded by French lawyer on the other side

blocks.note: short for avocat, the French word for a lawyer
anti means opposed, on the other side

explanation.surface: A French advocate for the opposing side presses for the case to move on.
explanation.definitionFit: Avanti is Italian for forward, a shout urging people to advance.

clue.text: The general population in Ireland wander round centre of Newtown willingly as before

indicators.note: round says the wandering word goes around what follows
the centre of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: to streel is Irish for to wander aimlessly
the fourth of seven letters
leve is an archaic form of lief, willingly

explanation.surface: Ordinary Irish people stroll around a new town, as willing as they used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Ireland' and 'as before' flag a dialect word and an archaism, not places or times.
explanation.definitionFit: Street level means the level of ordinary people, the grassroots of society.

clue.text: Rented accommodation for Jock to fumigate from bottom up

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the bottom up runs the word backwards

blocks.note: smoor is Scots for to smother, as with smoke; Jock is a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's lodgings need smoking out from floor to ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooms is the usual word for lodgings or a rented flat.

clue.text: Flap about fuel having to be sent back for old cargo boat

indicators.note: about says the flap goes around the fuel
sent back means turned round to read backwards

blocks.note: a tag is a loose flap or tab
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A fuss about fuel being returned for an old freighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A galiot was a small Dutch cargo vessel, or a light galley, now historic.

clue.text: Fleece? Mine's got a bit of tar on

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter
egg is old slang for a mine or bomb

explanation.surface: A sheep's fleece has picked up some tar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue puts the letter above the mine. The question mark flags the definition: a tegg is a two-year-old sheep, and the word also names its fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: Tegg is the term for a sheep in its second year and also for the wool shorn from it.

clue.text: Fool, one interested in birds losing beloved in Paris

indicators.note: losing says part of the bird-watcher's word is taken away

blocks.note: a twitcher is a keen birdwatcher
cher is French for dear, beloved

explanation.surface: A foolish birdwatcher has lost his sweetheart in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A twit is a silly or stupid person, the same as a fool.

clue.text: What sounds briefly like a major dish on the menu?

indicators.note: sounds tells you to go by how a phrase is said aloud

blocks.note: A major is a musical key; key of F is another, said briefly without the of

explanation.surface: A grand dish on the menu is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' tempts you to think of size or rank; it is a musical key, and 'briefly' drops the of from key of F.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken Kiev, a breaded chicken breast filled with garlic butter, is a familiar restaurant dish.

clue.text: Recall end of Bacchae, almost finished – their cry?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes
to recall is to call back, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: the final letter
over, finished, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Remembering the end of the Bacchae, a play nearly done: what did they shout?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their' refers to the Bacchae, Euripides' female followers of Bacchus, so the definition is their ritual shout.
explanation.definitionFit: Evoe was the cry of joy uttered by worshippers of Bacchus in their revels.

clue.text: Satellite, one inside – isn't it wrong way round?

indicators.note: inside puts one letter into the middle of the turned phrase
wrong way round means read from end to start

blocks.note: ain't it is the colloquial form of isn't it
A means one

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether a satellite has gone the wrong way round with one inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the largest moon of Uranus, a natural satellite named after Shakespeare's fairy queen.

clue.text: Fondle a pretty shell

blocks.note: to paw is to handle or fondle clumsily
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone handles a lovely shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawa, or paua, is the New Zealand abalone, whose iridescent shell is prized for ornaments.

clue.text: Order against striking disheartened thoroughfare

indicators.note: losing its heart means a word has its middle letters taken out

blocks.note: a street is a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: An order against a strike, with the high street demoralised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' suggests industrial action; it means striking out text, which an editor's mark cancels.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is a proofreader's instruction that a deleted passage should stand, so it countermands crossing out.

clue.text: Committing sin? Rag stirs seven, naughtily

indicators.note: acting naughtily means misbehaving, so the letters don't stay in line

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper stirs up seven people to behave badly.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a low-quality newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Transgressive means breaking a moral or legal rule, which is what sinning does.
